title: Seedless anchor experiments — quick notes
content:
Context:
- Trying a tiny experimental branch: remove explicit example seeds (no exemplar IDs, no metadata anchors) and rely on structural anchors instead (instructions + pattern examples). Goal: more robust few-shot that generalizes across domains with less brittle exemplar dependence.

Hypothesis:
- Removing exemplar seeds will reduce overfitting to example names/phrasing, but may increase hallucination if structure is weak. Need to compensate with stronger soft constraints.

Quick template ideas (seedless):
- Instruction header: 'Task: <one-line description> | Output format: <JSON/csv/short>'
- Pattern row: 'Input: <text>\nOutput: <expected label or structured snippet>' (repeat 2-3 pattern rows, no author names/dates)
- Final prompt: 'Now apply the pattern to this input: <user-input>'.

3-shot pattern (example):
1) Input: 'Order #49, shipped yesterday to 45 Bright Ave'
   Output: '{"type":"shipment","id":49,"status":"shipped"}'
2) Input: 'Refund 203 for customer Lydia; processed on 2025-10-10'
   Output: '{"type":"refund","id":203,"customer":"Lydia"}'
3) Input: 'Chargeback 12 — disputed, pending'
   Output: '{"type":"chargeback","id":12,"status":"pending"}'
--> Query: Input: '<user text here>'

Observed failure modes so far (notes):
- Pattern collapse: model copies structure but invents keys not shown ('amount','priority'). Appears when examples are sparse.
- Latent anchoring: even without explicit exemplar names, model latches onto lexical cues (dates -> status) and misapplies.
- Overgeneralization: for long inputs it drops nested items and flattens into a summary.

Example transcript with failure (raw):
- Prompt: [3 pattern rows above] + 'Input: Order 77; customer: Marco; delivered last week.\nOutput:'
- Model response: '{"type":"shipment","id":77,"status":"delivered","eta":"N/A","amount":"unknown"}'
- Issue: 'eta' and 'amount' were inferred despite never appearing in patterns.

Debug checklist (fast):
- [ ] Add one explicit negative example: show 'no-eta' -> '{"eta":null}' to discourage invention.
- [ ] Reduce temperature to 0.0-0.2; re-run 50 samples.
- [ ] Add explicit schema line (list allowed keys) before patterns.
- [ ] Try 4 shorter pattern rows vs 2 longer ones.
- [ ] Compare anchored vs seedless with same token budget.

Metrics I track manually for now:
- Hallucination rate (percent keys not present in examples)
- Schema adherence (exact match vs partial)
- Token-per-output and latency rough estimate
- Failure-class distribution (invented-keys, wrong-types, dropped-fields)

Next experiments (prioritized):
- Run A/B: seedless vs seeded (existing exemplar set) on 1k annotator-labelled inputs (use PR-1273 test harness).
- Insert explicit 'allowed_keys' line in prompt; measure reduction in invented keys.
- Try lightweight constraint by appending 'If unknown, return null' at end of examples.
- Evaluate with temperature sweep (0.0, 0.2, 0.6) and top-k/top-p if applicable.

Notes-to-self / brain dump:
- Might be advantage to use 'structural anchors' like consistent punctuation and line breaks rather than human metadata. Models pay attention to layout.
- Keep example language minimal and semantically generic to force pattern learning.
- Watch out for token budget: sometimes adding schema line reduces hallucination but increases tokens enough to push model into different behavior.

Pointers / links:
- Quick PR with harness + baseline: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-lab/pull/88
- Slack discussion thread: slack://channel/prompt-research/thread/CK12345
- Design doc (todo): confluence:PROMPT-ANCHORING

To do (short):
- [ ] Wire up PR-1273 dataset and run 500-input pilot seedless vs seeded. (Ethan to help with runner)
- [ ] Add negative-example row to template and iterate.
- [ ] Capture random failed examples into a small triage set for annotation.

End of scratchpad. Keep quick notes here and prune into formal doc if signal looks promising.
